---
title: "Mathematical Modeling with Technology"
subtitle: "Computational lectures for applied mathematics"
---

Welcome! This site collects lecture notebooks for a course in mathematical modeling, data analysis, and machine learning. The central idea is simple: use mathematics and computation together to investigate real-world phenomena.

## Start here

Use the navigation sidebar to move through the course, or begin with the [course preface](preface.qmd). Each lecture is a rendered Jupyter notebook with its explanations, equations, code, figures, and saved outputs.

The course is organized into four modules:

- **Time series and forecasting** - model and forecast future trends of seasonal (and non-seasonal) data with statistical and machine learning approaches.
- **Biology, disease, and systems** — translate mechanisms into differential and difference equations, then analyze and simulate them.
- **Data, similarity, and regression** — use linear algebra, SVD, PCA, and regression to discover structure in data.
- **Deep learning with PyTorch** — build intuition for tensors, automatic differentiation, optimization, and neural networks.

## Working with the notebooks

The pages are designed for reading, but the source notebooks are available from the repository links at the top of each page. Download a notebook to run it locally, or open it in Google Colab using the repository's notebook URL pattern:

```text
https://colab.research.google.com/github/mbanuelos/grad_math_modeling/blob/main/<path-to-notebook>
```

Some notebooks depend on data files stored beside them. Keep the repository folder structure intact when downloading the complete project.

::: {.callout-note}
## A note on reproducibility

The public book uses the outputs saved in the notebooks and does not execute Python during the GitHub Pages build. This keeps deployment reliable and makes the rendered lectures stable. Re-run notebooks locally when you want to update an experiment or regenerate a figure.
:::
